# MEMORANDUM

**To:** Owen Castellano, Partner
**From:** [Associate]
**Date:** November 17, 2026
**Re:** Diril Live Presents LLC / Kevond Staging & Production Services, Inc.: review of the production services contract file
**Privileged & Confidential: Attorney Work Product**

---

## 1. Summary

I reviewed all ten documents in the Kevond folder:

- the Master Services Agreement dated March 1, 2024 (the **MSA**), which is governed by New York law;
- the November 14, 2023 term sheet;
- the festival LED side letter;
- SOW No. 7 for the Ember Season 2027 North American Tour;
- Amendment No. 1;
- the production quality and safety agreement;
- the data processing addendum;
- the service level schedule;
- the September 16, 2026 production meeting notes; and
- Helena Marsh's November 2, 2026 email.

Under MSA Section 4.3, Diril must buy Services with Fees of at least **$4,200,000 per Contract Year** (the **Minimum Annual Commitment**). A Contract Year runs from March 1. The current Initial Term runs to **February 29, 2028**. Under MSA Section 2.3, the body of the MSA prevails over Amendment No. 1, the SOWs, the schedules and addenda, and the side letters.

I found four material issues. They are listed below in order of urgency.

| # | Issue | Where | Deadline / exposure |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The Pellbrook acquisition is a Change of Control deemed an assignment. It needs Kevond's prior written consent, and the MSA is missing from the consent list. | MSA §§ 1.1, 16.2, 16.3; GC email ¶ 2 | Closing **Dec. 15, 2026**; Pellbrook wants consents by **Dec. 8**. Without consent, Kevond can terminate and claim the Minimum Commitment Shortfall. |
| 2 | Diril's Reduction Notice was late, so on the face of the documents the 2027 commitment stays at $4.2M. | Amendment No. 1 § 3 | Window closed **Sept. 30, 2026**. Up to **$1.3M** is at stake. |
| 3 | "Provider Personnel" covers employees only, so the indemnity does not reach the independent-contractor Local Crew doing rigging, flying and pyrotechnics. | MSA §§ 1.1, 10.1; SOW No. 7 § 3.2 | Must be fixed before Ember rehearsals start on **Apr. 5, 2027**. Exposure is uncapped bodily injury and property damage risk. |
| 4 | The MSA auto-renews for three-year terms with a narrow non-renewal window. This departs from the term sheet. | MSA § 12.2; Term Sheet § 5 | Window is approx. **Nov. 1 to Dec. 1, 2027**. Missing it means **$12.6M** of further minimum spend. |

All four issues give Kevond leverage, or give Diril something to ask for. Kevond's consent to the Pellbrook deal is needed within the next three weeks. That makes the consent request the natural moment to negotiate a single Amendment No. 2 covering all four issues (see Section 4).

---

## 2. Issues

### Issue 1: Pellbrook acquisition triggers the Change of Control / assignment clause

**Where:**
- MSA Section 1.1, definition of "Change of Control," limb (b);
- MSA Section 16.2 (Client assignment);
- MSA Section 16.3 (remedy for unconsented assignment);
- GC email, paragraphs 2.1–2.4.

**What the documents say.**
- **Definition.** "Change of Control" includes "the acquisition by any person or group of more than 50% of the voting equity of any entity that directly or indirectly Controls Client."
- **Deemed assignment.** Section 16.2 bars Diril from assigning "by operation of law or otherwise" without Kevond's prior written consent. It also provides that "Any Change of Control of Client is deemed an assignment."
- **Affiliate exception.** The exception for assignment to an Affiliate expressly excludes an Affiliate "that is the subject of a Change of Control." It does not help here.
- **The deal.** The GC email reports that Pellbrook Live Group, Inc. will acquire **100%** of Diril Entertainment Holdings, Inc., Diril's sole parent. Closing is set for **December 15, 2026**.

That is a Change of Control under limb (b), and therefore a deemed assignment. It does not matter that Diril Live Presents LLC itself stays in place and that "no contracts will be assigned out of it." The MSA was drafted to catch exactly this indirect, parent-level transfer. The Kevond MSA does not appear on the consent list in paragraph 2.3 of the GC email.

**Why it matters to Diril Live.**
- **Termination right.** If closing occurs without Kevond's prior written consent, Section 16.3 lets Kevond terminate the MSA by notice within 90 days after it learns of the deal.
- **Shortfall payment.** Diril would then owe, within 30 days, all Fees for Services performed plus the **Minimum Commitment Shortfall**. That is the unmet Minimum Annual Commitment for the Contract Year in progress (March 2026 to February 2027) and for each remaining Contract Year of the then-current term.
- **Size of the exposure.** At a December 2026 closing, the remaining Contract Year is the one beginning March 1, 2027. Its commitment is $4.2M (if the reduction has lapsed, see Issue 2), less the roughly $593,400 SOW No. 7 deposit already invoiced. Together with any unmet balance for the current year, the claim could run to several million dollars.
- **No cap.** Section 14.3(d) carves the Minimum Commitment Shortfall out of the liability cap and the consequential damages exclusion, so the full amount is recoverable.
- **Tour risk.** Termination would remove Diril's main production vendor about four months before Ember Season rehearsals begin on April 5, 2027. The tour is Diril's largest 2027 commitment.
- **Leverage and confidentiality.** Even if Kevond does not terminate, the right gives it strong leverage in the commitment dispute (Issue 2). Pellbrook's confidentiality request (GC email ¶ 2.5) is not an obstacle: the request covers parties beyond the consent list, so adding Kevond to the list resolves it. Kevond is also bound by MSA Section 8.

**Recommended fix.**
1. **Flag this to Helena now.** Her November 9 comment deadline has passed. Ask that the Kevond MSA be added to the consent list immediately and that Pellbrook's deal counsel be told.
2. **Send a written consent request to Kevond this week**, addressed under MSA Section 18.2 to Kevond's President. The aim is a signed consent in hand before the December 8 target and in any event before closing.
3. **Ask for the right content in the consent.** It should:
   - consent to the Pellbrook transaction as a Change of Control under Section 16.2;
   - expressly waive Kevond's termination and Minimum Commitment Shortfall rights under Section 16.3 for this transaction; and
   - confirm the MSA and SOW No. 7 continue in full force.

   Section 18.3 requires any waiver to be in writing.
4. **Protect the SPA position.** Coordinate with deal counsel so that the stock purchase agreement disclosure schedules list the Kevond consent. Treat it as a required consent and do not close over it.
5. **Prepare for Kevond's asks.** Kevond will likely try to use the request to settle the reduction dispute on its terms. Decide the negotiating position on Issues 2–4 before sending the request (see Section 4).

### Issue 2: Reduction Notice delivered after the 60-day window closed

**Where:**
- Amendment No. 1, Section 3 (in particular Sections 3.1 and 3.5), read with Section 1.1 (Amendment Effective Date);
- GC email, paragraphs 3.1–3.5.

**What the documents say.**
- **The right.** Section 3.1 gives Diril a one-time right to reduce the 2027 Contract Year Minimum Annual Commitment from $4,200,000 to $2,900,000. Diril exercises it by a Reduction Notice "delivered within 60 days after the Amendment Effective Date."
- **The window.** The Amendment Effective Date is **August 1, 2026**, so the window closed on **September 30, 2026**.
- **The notice.** Diril delivered its notice on **October 9, 2026**, nine days late.
- **Default rule.** Section 3.5 provides that, absent a notice "in accordance with Sections 3.1 and 3.2," the commitment "remains $4,200,000."
- **Kevond's position.** Kevond rejected the notice as untimely on October 20, 2026.
- **Diril's position.** Diril has disputed the rejection in writing and has not signed anything accepting the $4.2M figure.

**Why it matters to Diril Live.** On the face of the documents, the reduction right has lapsed and Kevond can hold Diril to $4.2M for the Contract Year starting March 1, 2027. The headline difference is **$1.3M**. In practice, the exposure is the gap between Diril's actual 2027 Kevond spend and $4.2M, not the full $1.3M:
- SOW No. 7 alone carries estimated Fees of $3,379,000, all counting toward that Contract Year (SOW § 1.3; Amendment § 3.4(c)).
- At $2.9M, Ember Season alone would have satisfied the commitment.
- At $4.2M, Diril must place about **$821,000** of further Kevond work in that year or pay the difference at the § 4.4 true-up.
- Kevond-attributable cancellations reduce the commitment, but Diril's own cancellations do not (§ 13.3).

**Assessment of Diril's arguments.** New York courts generally require options of this kind to be exercised strictly within their terms. The arguments are real but uphill.

- **Waiver.** This argument is weak.
  - MSA Section 18.3 requires waivers in writing.
  - It also says delay in exercising a right is not a waiver.
  - Kevond rejected the notice within 11 days of receiving it.
- **Estoppel.** This is the better argument, but it is fact-dependent. Helena reports that Kevond discussed 2027 slate planning with the CFO's team in late September, inside the window, without raising timing. Estoppel requires conduct by Kevond that Diril reasonably relied on in letting the deadline pass. Silence or ordinary planning talks may not be enough. We need the actual communications.
- **Ordinary course dealings.** Continued production work on Ember Season is consistent with the MSA either way and adds little.

**Recommended fix.**
1. **Do not concede.** Keep the written reservation of rights in place and do not sign or accept any invoice, true-up statement or document that confirms $4.2M.
2. **Collect the evidence.** This means:
   - the late-September emails and meeting notes with the CFO's team;
   - any Kevond statements about 2027 volumes or the reduction; and
   - Kevond's October 20 letter.

   We should then give a firmer view on estoppel.
3. **Resolve it commercially, as Helena prefers.** Seek an Amendment No. 2 that either:
   - extends the reduction deadline nunc pro tunc and accepts the October 9 notice; or
   - agrees a compromise figure (e.g., $3.4M–$3.6M, broadly matching Ember Season plus planned festival work).

   This fits naturally alongside the Pellbrook consent (Issue 1).
4. **Prepare a fallback.** In parallel, have the touring team identify 2027 engagements that could be routed to Kevond to use any remaining commitment rather than pay a true-up.

### Issue 3: "Provider Personnel" excludes contractors, leaving a gap in the indemnity

**Where:**
- MSA Section 1.1, definition of "Provider Personnel";
- MSA Section 10.1;
- SOW No. 7, Section 3.2.

**What the documents say.**
- **The definition.** MSA Section 1.1 defines "Provider Personnel" as "individuals employed by Provider who perform Services."
- **The indemnity.** Kevond's bodily injury and property damage indemnity in Section 10.1 covers losses "caused by the negligence or willful misconduct of Provider or Provider Personnel."
- **The SOW.** SOW No. 7, Section 3.2 says all rigging, flying and pyrotechnic work on the Tour will be performed by "Provider Personnel, including the Local Crew engaged by Provider as independent contractors." It defines Local Crew as the up riggers, down riggers, fly operators and pyrotechnic technicians Kevond engages at each Venue.
- **Precedence.** The SOW treats contractors as Provider Personnel. The MSA does not. Section 2.3 gives the MSA precedence, so the employee-only definition controls Section 10.1.

**Why it matters to Diril Live.**
- **Highest-risk work uncovered.** Overhead rigging, performer flying and pyrotechnics are the tour's highest-risk activities. If a Local Crew rigger's negligence causes a dropped object or a pyro injury, Kevond can argue that the claim falls outside Section 10.1 unless Kevond itself (e.g., its supervision) was negligent.
- **No general fallback.** Under New York law, a party that hires an independent contractor is generally not liable for the contractor's negligence. Nothing else in the MSA makes Kevond answerable for its subcontractors, as Section 3.5 deals only with coordinating local labor.
- **Who bears the claim.** Diril, as promoter, will be named in any third-party claim. It could end up bearing the loss without contractual recourse.
- **Ripple effects.** The same definition limits the qualification duties in MSA Section 5.1 and the certification duties in Quality Agreement Section 3.1.
- **Related inconsistency.** Quality Agreement Section 3.3 says Kevond "shall not assign local labor to performer flying or to pyrotechnic firing." Yet the SOW defines Local Crew to include fly operators and pyrotechnic technicians. Kevond may be planning a staffing model the Quality Agreement prohibits. Under Quality Agreement Section 1.3, the stricter requirement should apply, but the point should be clarified.

**Recommended fix.** Fix this by amendment before the April 5, 2027 rehearsals, either in Amendment No. 2 or a short standalone amendment.

1. **Redefine "Provider Personnel"** to mean "individuals employed or engaged by Provider or by any of its subcontractors (including Local Crew) who perform Services."
2. **Add a responsibility clause** making Kevond responsible for the acts and omissions of its subcontractors and contractors as if they were its own.
3. **Amend Section 10.1** to cover negligence or willful misconduct of "Provider, its subcontractors, or any Provider Personnel."
4. **Address insurance:**
   - Confirm in writing that Kevond's CGL and umbrella policies (MSA § 11.1) cover liability for contractor work.
   - Require Kevond either to cover Local Crew under its policies or to obtain certificates from contractors naming Diril as additional insured.
5. **Deal with Venue house labor separately.** Labor that a Venue's collective bargaining agreement requires (SOW § 3.5) can be carved out, because it is engaged by the Venue rather than Kevond.
6. **Confirm the staffing plan.** Get Kevond's written confirmation that performer flying and pyrotechnic firing will be done only by touring crew, consistent with Quality Agreement Section 3.3.

### Issue 4: Automatic three-year renewal departs from the term sheet

**Where:**
- MSA Section 12.2;
- Term Sheet, Section 5.2.

**What the documents say.**
- **Auto-renewal.** At the end of the Initial Term (February 29, 2028), the MSA "will automatically renew for successive three-year periods."
- **Narrow notice window.** Non-renewal requires written notice "delivered not more than 120 days nor fewer than 90 days before the end of the then-current term." A notice outside that window "is of no effect."
- **Commitment carries forward.** The $4.2M Minimum Annual Commitment applies to every Contract Year of each Renewal Term.
- **The agreed deal was different.** Term Sheet Section 5.2 provided that the MSA "may be extended by one-year renewals only by mutual written agreement," after a meeting on pricing, the minimum commitment and scope.

**Why it matters to Diril Live.**
- **Large lock-in.** If the roughly 30-day window is missed, Diril is locked in for three more years at $4.2M a year, a total of **$12.6M** of minimum spend.
- **Repeats every cycle.** The same trap recurs each renewal cycle.
- **The term sheet does not help.** It is expressly non-binding except for Section 12, and it is not among the contract documents. MSA Section 2.3 also gives the MSA body top precedence, so the term sheet cannot override Section 12.2.
- **Larger shortfall claims.** A renewal would also extend "the then-current term" for the Minimum Commitment Shortfall under Section 16.3. That would increase any future unconsented-assignment claim.

**Recommended fix.**
1. **Diarize the window now.** Counting back from February 29, 2028, the window runs approximately **November 1 to December 1, 2027**. Plan to deliver notice by courier and email under Section 18.2 around **mid-November 2027**, and confirm receipt. If Diril wants to keep the relationship, a protective non-renewal notice still preserves the option to renegotiate.
2. **Seek an amendment to Section 12.2** to conform to the term sheet: one-year renewals only by mutual written agreement, with no automatic renewal. As a fallback, ask for:
   - one-year automatic renewals;
   - a non-renewal right exercisable at any time up to 60–90 days before expiry; and
   - re-pricing of the minimum commitment on renewal.
3. **Use the moment.** Raise this in the same Amendment No. 2 negotiation, while Kevond wants to keep the Ember Season relationship and the Pellbrook-enlarged business.

---

## 3. Other observations (lower priority)

- **Side letter rates expire with the Initial Term.** The festival LED rates apply only to Engagements whose first show date falls in the Initial Term (Side Letter § 1.1). They also rank last in precedence. Any renewal negotiation should carry them forward expressly.
- **Service credits are modest.** Credits are capped at 15% of monthly production fees (SLS § 4.1), and Fees count toward the Minimum Annual Commitment before credits (SLS § 6.2). They give limited leverage, but Diril's other remedies are preserved (SLS § 6.3).
- **Void-assignment wording.** Section 16.3 says an unconsented "purported assignment" is void. Applied to a deemed assignment by Change of Control, the wording is awkward. Kevond's realistic remedy is termination plus shortfall. This is another reason to get clean written consent.
- **No issues found** in the data processing addendum or the September 2026 production meeting notes. The notes confirm the tour is proceeding normally and that they do not amend the MSA or SOW.

## 4. Suggested approach

1. **This week:**
   - Advise Helena on Issue 1.
   - Have the MSA added to the consent list.
   - Send Kevond's consent request.
2. **In parallel:**
   - Gather the September communications for the estoppel argument (Issue 2).
   - Prepare a draft Amendment No. 2 covering:
     - the Change of Control consent and Section 16.3 waiver;
     - resolution of the 2027 commitment;
     - the Provider Personnel and indemnity fix; and
     - conforming the renewal mechanism to the term sheet.
3. **Calendar:**
   - **December 8, 2026:** consent target.
   - **April 5, 2027:** indemnity fix in place before rehearsals.
   - **November 1 to December 1, 2027:** non-renewal window.

Happy to discuss before the call with Helena and Daniel.

I reviewed all ten documents in the Kevond file. Three issues need action. One of them must be resolved within the next three weeks.

| # | Issue | Where | Urgency |
|---|---|---|---|

## 2. Issues

### Issue 1: Pellbrook acquisition triggers the MSA's change-of-control / assignment provision

**Where it appears**
- MSA Section 1.1, definition of "Change of Control," limb (b): "the acquisition by any person or group of more than 50% of the voting equity of any entity that directly or indirectly Controls Client."
- MSA Section 16.2: Diril may not assign "by operation of law or otherwise" without Kevond's prior written consent. "Any Change of Control of Client is deemed an assignment."
- MSA Section 16.3: an unconsented deemed assignment lets Kevond terminate and claim the Minimum Commitment Shortfall.
- GC email (D10), Paragraph 2: Pellbrook Live Group, Inc. will acquire 100% of Diril Entertainment Holdings, Inc., with closing on **December 15, 2026**. The consent list at ¶ 2.3 does not include the Kevond MSA.

**Why it matters to Diril Live**
- The GC's email reasons that Diril Live Presents LLC "will stay in place as the contracting entity" and "no contracts will be assigned out of it." That reasoning does not work under this MSA. Limb (b) of the definition expressly covers an acquisition of the *parent*. Holdings wholly owns, and so Controls, Diril Live, so Pellbrook's purchase of 100% of Holdings is a Change of Control of Client. Section 16.2 then **deems** that Change of Control an assignment, whether or not any contract actually moves.
- The affiliate carve-out in Section 16.2 does not help. It applies only to an assignment to an Affiliate "that is not the subject of a Change of Control."
- If closing occurs without Kevond's prior written consent, Section 16.3 gives Kevond three things:
  - a right to terminate by notice within 90 days after it learns of the transaction;
  - payment within 30 days of all Fees for Services performed; and
  - payment of the **Minimum Commitment Shortfall**. This is the unmet minimum for the Contract Year in progress *and* each remaining Contract Year in the then-current term. On a December 2026 closing, that covers the balance of the current Contract Year (ending February 28, 2027) and the full 2027 Contract Year (March 1, 2027 to February 29, 2028), less Fees invoiced. Depending on what has been invoiced, the exposure could approach the full $4.2M for 2027 plus any shortfall for the current year.
- Section 14.3(d) carves the Minimum Commitment Shortfall out of the liability cap.
- Section 16.3 also says a purported assignment in breach is "void." Kevond could use that to unsettle the relationship generally.
- Kevond is Diril's main production vendor and is crewing Ember Season, Diril's largest 2027 tour. A termination right in Kevond's hands just before rehearsals start in April 2027 would give Kevond substantial leverage.
- The GC asked for comments on the consent list by November 9. That date has passed, so this point should go to the client immediately.

**Recommended fix**
1. **Tell the GC and the deal team now.** Add the Kevond MSA to the consent list in GC email ¶ 2.3.
2. **Request Kevond's prior written consent** to the Change of Control as soon as possible, and well before the December 8 consent deadline. The consent should be signed by an authorized Kevond officer, given Section 18.3 (written amendments and waivers). It should:
   - consent expressly to the Pellbrook transaction as a Change of Control under Section 16.2;
   - waive Kevond's termination and shortfall rights under Section 16.3 for this transaction; and
   - confirm that the MSA, Amendment No. 1 and SOW No. 7 continue in full force.
3. **Confidentiality.** Section 8 of the MSA protects disclosure to Kevond, and Pellbrook has asked that the transaction be shared only with counterparties on the consent list. Adding Kevond to the list resolves this. Confirm with Pellbrook's counsel before the request goes out.
4. **Expect Kevond to use this as leverage**, including on the 2027 commitment dispute (Issue 2). Decide the negotiating position on both issues together before approaching Kevond (see Section 3 below).
5. **Fallback.** If consent cannot be obtained by closing, raise it with Pellbrook. Options include a closing condition, a specific indemnity or escrow in the SPA, or deferring closing. Do not close quietly and rely on Kevond not noticing. The 90-day clock runs from when Kevond *learns* of the transaction, and the deal will be publicly announced at closing.
6. **Going forward.** In any future amendment, seek to narrow the Change of Control definition so that it excludes upstream transactions where Diril Live remains the contracting entity, or at least cap the remedy.

---

### Issue 2: The Reduction Notice was delivered after the 60-day window closed

**Where it appears**
- Amendment No. 1 Section 3.1: Diril may reduce the 2027 Contract Year Minimum Annual Commitment from $4,200,000 to $2,900,000 by a Reduction Notice "delivered within 60 days after the Amendment Effective Date." The Amendment Effective Date is August 1, 2026 (§ 1.1).
- Amendment No. 1 Section 3.5: if no Reduction Notice is delivered in accordance with Sections 3.1 and 3.2, the 2027 commitment "remains $4,200,000."
- GC email (D10), Paragraph 3: the Reduction Notice was delivered October 9, 2026, and Kevond rejected it as untimely on October 20, 2026.

**Why it matters to Diril Live**
- Sixty days after August 1, 2026 is **September 30, 2026**. The notice went out on **October 9, 2026**, nine days late.
- On the face of the documents, the one-time right has lapsed. Section 3.5 states the consequence expressly, so Kevond's position is strong on the text. The amount in dispute is $1,300,000 of 2027 commitment.
- **The real cash exposure is probably smaller than $1.3M:**
  - Ember Season SOW No. 7 Fees, estimated at $3,379,000, count toward the 2027 Contract Year (SOW § 1.3; Amendment § 3.4(c)).
  - Against a $4.2M commitment, Ember alone leaves a gap of about $821,000 before any other 2027 SOWs (festivals, single events).
  - The finance team should model the true expected true-up under Section 4.4 on the actual 2027 slate. That figure is the realistic amount at stake.
- **Possible arguments for Diril:**
  - The GC reports that Kevond kept engaging on the reduction and discussed 2027 slate planning with the CFO's team in late September. Kevond did not raise timing until October 20.
  - That conduct may support waiver or estoppel arguments under New York law.
  - These arguments are uphill. MSA Section 18.3 provides that "No waiver is effective unless in writing" and that delay does not operate as a waiver. New York courts generally enforce such clauses, although they can be overcome by clear conduct. Estoppel would require showing that Diril relied to its detriment on Kevond's conduct in *not* serving the notice before September 30.
  - The internal approval did not come until early October, and that weakens the reliance story.
- Diril has not signed anything accepting $4.2M and has disputed Kevond's rejection in writing. That preserves the position, and Diril should not concede.

**Recommended fix**
1. **Advise the client candidly.** Textually, the right has lapsed and Kevond's rejection is well-founded. Waiver and estoppel are negotiating arguments, not strong litigation positions.
2. **Gather the evidence now.** This includes:
   - the late-September communications between Kevond and the CFO's team;
   - any Kevond statements acknowledging the reduction; and
   - Kevond's October 20 letter (the GC has offered to send it).

   Any written Kevond statement that treated the reduction as still open would materially strengthen the waiver argument.
3. **Pursue a commercial resolution through a short Amendment No. 2.** Options include:
   - a late-exercise acceptance;
   - a split reduction, for example to $3.5M;
   - a carry-forward of unused 2027 commitment into a later year; or
   - crediting Ember change orders or added dates toward the commitment.

   This matches the GC's stated preference to avoid Section 17.3 escalation.
4. **Coordinate with Issue 1.** Kevond will likely price its change-of-control consent. Consider presenting a single package: consent to the Pellbrook transaction plus a negotiated 2027 commitment figure. Alternatively, firmly keep the two issues separate if Diril would rather not trade them. That is a client decision, but it should be made deliberately and before the consent request goes out.
5. **Do not sign** any document, true-up acknowledgment or invoice confirmation that recites $4.2M for 2027 while discussions continue. Reserve rights in correspondence.

---

### Issue 3: Automatic three-year renewal with a narrow non-renewal window, contrary to the term sheet

**Where it appears**
- MSA Section 12.2: at the end of the Initial Term (February 29, 2028), the MSA "will automatically renew for successive three-year periods." Non-renewal notice must be "delivered not more than 120 days nor fewer than 90 days before the end of the then-current term," and a notice outside that period "is of no effect." The Section 4.3 Minimum Annual Commitment applies to every Contract Year of each Renewal Term.
- Term Sheet (D2) Section 5.2: after the Initial Term, the MSA "may be extended by one-year renewals only by mutual written agreement," with a meeting beforehand to discuss pricing, the minimum commitment and scope.

**Why it matters to Diril Live**
- The MSA reverses the agreed deal. The parties agreed to an opt-in, one-year, mutually agreed renewal. The MSA instead has an opt-out, three-year, automatic renewal.
- If Diril misses a window of roughly 30 days, it is locked into three more years at $4,200,000 per year. That is a **$12.6M minimum spend**, with no built-in renegotiation of pricing or scope.
- On my count the window runs from approximately **November 1, 2027 to December 1, 2027**. The calendar should confirm the exact dates, measuring back from February 29, 2028.
  - A notice sent early is void, just as a late one is.
  - Notice must comply with Section 18.2 (hand, courier, or email with courier confirmation) and is effective on receipt.
- The term sheet does not help. It is expressly non-binding except for Section 12, and MSA Section 2.3 makes the MSA prevail in any event.
- The narrowness of the window is also a concern given what happened with the Reduction Notice (Issue 2). A missed deadline is a demonstrated risk for this client.
- There is a related point on the side letter. The festival LED side letter rates apply only to Engagements whose first show date falls within the *Initial Term* (Side Letter § 1.1). An automatic renewal would therefore carry forward the commitment without the negotiated LED/video pricing.
- If Pellbrook's ownership changes Diril's vendor strategy, an unwanted three-year lock-in could limit the new group's flexibility.
